variants.specifics: Brackenford: Reeve Halvard, fussy, bargains for the stolen tithe chest and hands over the watchtower cellar key; Sly Wat posts his own bounty on Nettle Hob, dead or alive.

offer_a.speaker: Halvard
offer_a.text:
Ah. Hello. I presuppose you have come concerning the tithe.

Very well. If you will fetch back the tithe chest those nefarious bandits carried off, I will see you paid in full, and promptly. Here, take this iron key. It opens the cellar under the old watchtower. They will have put the chest down there, I am quite certain.

offer_b.speaker: Wat
offer_b.text:
Halvard's men won't go near Crow Hill. So I'm putting up my own bounty.

There's a fellow up there called Nettle Hob. He threw me out of Corwin's band and kept my share, didn't he? Bring him down here alive and I'll pay you 60 gold. Dead, 30. Alive is better. I want to see his face.

outcome_a.speaker: Halvard
outcome_a.text: The tithe chest! Is it all there? ... Yes. Yes, all there. Most satisfactory! Your reward is 120 gold pieces.

outcome_b.speaker: Wat
outcome_b.text: Hob! Look at him! Oh, this is a happy day. Here's your gold, as agreed.

journal_a.text: Recover the tithe chest from the old watchtower on Crow Hill.

journal_b.text: Bring Nettle Hob to Sly Wat, dead or alive.

variants.specifics: Bormunt: Velgard, a gruff old wizard, orders the player to get back his Spell Lantern from the Urchins and teaches a spell; Ludo Quickpurse sells a dead man's Chain Tunic for 50 gold (the player pays).

offer_a.speaker: Velgard
offer_a.text: Hmph! Robbed! In my own house?! Those blasted Urchins have taken my Spell Lantern, and with Skarn's Trolls about I need it more than ever. Get it back. I'll teach you a spell for your trouble.

offer_b.speaker: Ludo Quickpurse
offer_b.text: Ahhh, a customer! Lookee here, a Chain Tunic, hardly worn! The last owner was buried in it, but he didn't move around much after that, so it's good as new! Yours for 50 gold. That's half what Hask asks!

outcome_a.speaker: Velgard
outcome_a.text: Hmph. My Lantern. Took you long enough. Well, a promise is a promise, sit down and I'll teach you that spell.

outcome_b.speaker: Ludo Quickpurse
outcome_b.text: A fine bargain, friend! Come back anytime, I get new stock every week.

journal_a.text: Recover Velgard's Spell Lantern from the Urchins.

journal_b.text: Buy the used Chain Tunic from Ludo Quickpurse.

variants.specifics: Oskry: Sister Ondine wants the Sacred Bell back from the Sunken Shrine and gives the shrine key at once (pays with a spell she teaches); Snig the smuggler will row the player there if Mayor Brumm signs his petition to unchain his boats.

offer_a.speaker: Sister Ondine
offer_a.text: Oh! Kind sir! Help me, I beg of you! The abominable dead have besieged our Sunken Shrine, and the Sacred Bell of Oskry lies abandoned within, at the mercy of that nefarious witch Vesra! If you could recover it, you would deliver this entire village from ruin. Here, take this silver key. It will unlock the shrine doors.

offer_b.speaker: Snig
offer_b.text:
You want to get out to the Sunken Shrine? Nobody gets there without a boat, and nobody's got boats but me. Only the Mayor went and chained them all up. Says I'm a smuggler.

Get Mayor Brumm to put his mark on this petition and I'll row you out there myself. Free!

outcome_a.speaker: Sister Ondine
outcome_a.text:
The Sacred Bell! It has been restored to us! Oskry is forever in your debt, kind sir.

As I vowed, I shall teach you a spell of great power. May it serve you well against the Undead.

outcome_b.speaker: Snig
outcome_b.text: His mark, right there! Ha! My boats are mine again. Climb in whenever you like, I'll take you anywhere.

journal_a.text: Recover the Sacred Bell from the Sunken Shrine.

journal_b.text: Get Mayor Brumm to sign Snig's petition.

variants.specifics: Castle Brask: Armsmaster Krell wants the beacon on Gallow Crag lit again; Velka the smuggler wants her friend Tibbet broken out of the castle cells.

offer_a.speaker: Armsmaster Krell
offer_a.text: Greetings, Wanderer. Here's my offer. You do a job for me, and I'll find you something good in the armoury. The beacon on Gallow Crag, west across the river, has gone dark. The men I sent up to light it haven't come back. Light it again. Will you?

offer_b.speaker: Velka
offer_b.text: You! Yes, you. Come over here, and keep your voice down. My friend Tibbet is locked in the castle cells and they mean to hang him on market day. The jailer sleeps after his supper and leaves his keys on a nail by the door. Get Tibbet out and I'll give you a steel shield. A good one.

outcome_a.speaker: Armsmaster Krell
outcome_a.text: The beacon's burning! I saw it from the wall. Good work. Here, take this sword. We pulled it out of the moat last spring and nobody ever claimed it.

outcome_b.speaker: Velka
outcome_b.text:
Tibbet! Ha! Look at you, all skin and bones!

Here's your shield, as I promised. If the guards ask, you never saw us.

journal_a.text: Light the beacon on Gallow Crag for Armsmaster Krell.

journal_b.text: Break Tibbet out of the castle cells.

variants.specifics: Vesk: Pruitt the Lamplighter, driven from his lighthouse by the dead, wants the Beacon Lens brought back; Bodkin Mudd wants to sell his house on stilts for 40,000 gold.

offer_a.speaker: Pruitt the Lamplighter
offer_a.text: Gaaahhh! Stay back! Stay back! ... Oh. Oh, you're alive. Forgive me, I took you for one of the dead. Go to my lighthouse on the north point and bring me the Beacon Lens. They drove me out before I could take it. Without the light our boats can't find their way home at night. And mind you don't drop it! It's very old.

offer_b.speaker: Bodkin Mudd
offer_b.text: Say, stranger! You look like somebody who needs a house! I got just the one. Up on stilts, right out over the lake, and the fish jump right into yer kitchen! Yours for 40,000 gold. A steal!

outcome_a.speaker: Pruitt the Lamplighter
outcome_a.text: The Beacon Lens! Not even cracked! Here are 150 gold pieces for your trouble. Tonight the light burns again!

outcome_b.speaker: Bodkin Mudd
outcome_b.text: Back for the house, are ya? Ha, ha... Funny story. She sank last night, stilts and all! Still want her? I'll knock off a hundred gold.

journal_a.text: Bring the Beacon Lens back to Pruitt the Lamplighter.

journal_b.text: Buy Bodkin Mudd's house for 40,000 gold.

variants.specifics: Vorne: Lissra, a nervous keeper of the Lyceum's treasures, lost the Moonstone to a Ghost in the chapel crypt and sends the player on to Master Dorrovan; Zabbo at the Singing Kettle bets 100 gold against 50 that nobody can ring the Clock Tower bell.

offer_a.speaker: Lissra
offer_a.text: Help! Oh, help me, please! The Moonstone! A Ghost came right through the chapel wall and snatched it out of my hands! I was only carrying it to Master Dorrovan... He'll be furious! It went down into the crypt beneath the chapel, I saw it go. I'll teach you a spell, a good one, if you bring it back. Please, will you?

offer_b.speaker: Zabbo
offer_b.text: Care for a wager, stranger? Nobody's rung the bell up in the Clock Tower since the Imps moved in. I'll put up 100 gold against your 50 that you can't do it either. Well? Is it a bet?

outcome_a.speaker: Lissra
outcome_a.text:
The Moonstone! Oh, thank goodness, thank goodness! Here is the spell I promised you.

And please... Master Dorrovan wishes to see you. He waits for you on the Lyceum steps.

outcome_b.speaker: Zabbo
outcome_b.text: That was you ringing the bell? I nearly fell off my stool! All right, all right, here's your gold. You won it fair.

journal_a.text: Recover the Moonstone from the crypt beneath the chapel.

journal_b.text: Ring the bell in the Clock Tower to win Zabbo's wager.

variants.specifics: Fort Kholm: Wendric the Priest gives the key to the chapel vault the Undead have desecrated; Lucky Skiv bets the player won't come back up.

offer_a.speaker: Wendric
offer_a.text:
Good day. I trust you are here regarding the chapel vault. The Undead broke into the vault beneath this chapel and desecrated the tombs of the fort's honored dead. I have barred the door, but I lack the strength to purge the abominable things myself.

Here, take this iron key, it opens the vault door behind the altar. Will you go down and cleanse the vault?

offer_b.speaker: Lucky Skiv
offer_b.text: Going down into Wendric's vault, are you? Ha! I'll wager you 100 gold you don't come back up. Do we have a bet?

outcome_a.speaker: Wendric
outcome_a.text: The vault is quiet once more! Our honored dead may rest in peace. Take this shield, with the blessing of the chapel. And go see Marshal Odric, he will want to hear of this.

outcome_b.speaker: Lucky Skiv
outcome_b.text: You?! Back from the vault, and not a scratch?! Well, I never welsh on a wager. Here's your 100 gold. Don't tell the others.

journal_a.text: Cleanse the chapel vault of the Undead for Wendric.

journal_b.text: Come back alive from the chapel vault and collect on Skiv's bet.

variants.specifics: Fornath: Priestess Velda wants the Great Bell back from the Ogre camp and pays with a spell; Warden Grubb puts a dead-or-alive bounty on Bram Sootfinger, who sells Fornath swords to the Ogres.

offer_a.speaker: Velda
offer_a.text: Ogres! Ogres in the Fire Shrine! They've carried off the Great Bell! Every forge in Fornath is lit at the ringing of that bell! Go east past the lava falls to the Ogre camp and bring it back. I'll teach you a fine spell for your trouble.

offer_b.speaker: Grubb
offer_b.text:
Bram Sootfinger has been selling our swords to the Ogres, the dirty rat! He's hiding out somewhere in the old furnace tunnels.

Bring him to me alive and I'll pay you 150 gold. Dead, 75. I'd rather have him alive... I've got a cell all swept out for him.

outcome_a.speaker: Velda
outcome_a.text:
The Great Bell! You brought it home! Oh, the smiths will be so glad!

Now, a spell for you, as I said. Hold still... There! It is yours, brave Adventurer.

outcome_b.speaker: Grubb
outcome_b.text:
Alive, eh? Good work! In you go, Bram.

Here's your gold. 150 pieces, count them if you like.

journal_a.text: Bring the Great Bell back to Priestess Velda.

journal_b.text: Capture Bram Sootfinger for Warden Grubb, dead or alive.

variants.specifics: Wendle Cross: Ambrus, a fussy scholar, wants the Book of Old Roads fetched from the chapel crypt for Telmarq; Warden Holk wants Grubbin the Grave-Robber back, dead or alive.

offer_a.speaker: Ambrus
offer_a.text:
Oh, botheration! Telmarq's sent someone after his book again?!

Very well, very well. When the Skeletons came up out of the chapel crypt I ran, and I left the Book of Old Roads down there on the reading stand. Telmarq says he can't find the way into Fort Skarrow without it. If you could get it back, you'd save my good name. Here, take this iron key. It opens the crypt door behind the chapel.

offer_b.speaker: Holk
offer_b.text: Wanted, dead or alive! Grubbin the Grave-Robber dug himself out of my cell last night. That wretch has been selling our dead to Zelloc by the cartload. He's hiding out on the Grey Moor somewhere. Bring him back alive and it's 100 gold. Dead, 50. Makes no difference to me, stranger.

outcome_a.speaker: Ambrus
outcome_a.text: My Book! Not a page torn! Oh, thank goodness. Telmarq shall have it tonight. Please, take this as a token of my appreciation.

outcome_b.speaker: Holk
outcome_b.text: Grubbin! Back in my cell where he belongs! Here's your 100 gold, as I promised. This time I'll chain him to the wall.

journal_a.text: Recover the Book of Old Roads from the chapel crypt for Ambrus.

journal_b.text: Bring Grubbin the Grave-Robber to Warden Holk, dead or alive.

variants.specifics: Hestle: Bramwell, a farmer, wants the Ogres run out of his barn; Sabble, a cider smuggler, wants his partner Rook broken out of the cellar under the Town Hall.

offer_a.speaker: Bramwell
offer_a.text:
Help! Ogres! There's Ogres in my barn!

They broke in last night. They've eaten the hay and now they're sleeping on what's left. I can't get near the place.

I'll tell you what. Run them off and I'll give you the old shield off my wall. Here's the key, the barn's west of the well. Go round the back.

offer_b.speaker: Sabble
offer_b.text:
Ahhh, now there's a face I can do business with! My partner Rook is locked up in Mayor Dulvane's cellar for carrying a few barrels of cider past the Ogres without paying the Mayor his tax, which is only a crime in Hestle and only since last spring and anyway somebody had to bring the cider in because nobody else would go near that road.

The cellar window at the back of the Town Hall has a loose bar. Pull it out and Rook can squeeze through.

You get him out, I'll find you something nice from the last load. No questions asked.

outcome_a.speaker: Bramwell
outcome_a.text:
My barn! They're gone! Thank you, thank you!

Here's the shield, as I promised. It came up out of my turnip field one spring. Never did find out whose it was.

outcome_b.speaker: Sabble
outcome_b.text: Rook's out?! Hah! Good work, friend! Here, this chain tunic is yours. Now I'd best go find him before the Mayor does.

journal_a.text: Drive the Ogres out of Bramwell's barn.

journal_b.text: Get Rook the smuggler out of the cellar under the Town Hall.
